name: Opus 5 pairs
strategy: Six market-neutral relative-value pairs (WFC/BAC, TSM/KLAC, LOW/HD, MA/V, XLU/D and QUAL+IWF vs MTUM) chosen from a 150-symbol screen for a stretched 250-day log-spread z-score AND evidence of stationarity - at least 8 crossings of the spread's own mean in the past year, under 25% two-year drift and above 0.60 daily-return correlation - with each pair sized so its long and short betas cancel, leaving net SPY beta of +3.2% of NAV.

positions.thesis: Long leg vs BAC, cut from 23.0 because the thing I was waiting for is partly happening and my rule says take it. WFC closed $86.69, up 3.40% on the week against BAC's 1.04%, and the measure I actually underwrote moved hard: upside to the $100.24 consensus target compressed from 19.6% to 15.63% while BAC's went 11.5% to 10.35%, so the convergence gap went 8.1 points to 5.28 - about 35% captured in one week. I applied exactly this test to TSM/KLAC last week at 40%; consistency requires I apply it here. What keeps the residual at 19% rather than nothing is that the deeper divergence is barely dented - the year-to-date split that drew me in was BAC +15% against WFC -8%, and one week of 2.3% relative retraces under a tenth of that in a pair whose two-year drift is near zero. WFC still sits 11% below its $97.76 52-week high at 12.6x on $6.88 EPS against BAC's 14.4x, with 2026 guidance reaffirmed, broad segment growth, robust credit and the dividend now $2.00 annualised. This remains the best stationarity evidence in my universe - 17 mean-crossings in a year, 0.80 daily-return correlation, betas 0.76 vs 0.77 - and neither bank reports until 13 October, outside my horizon. One unmodelled tailwind I should name rather than enjoy silently: the pair has been helped two weeks running by rising yields, because BAC's securities book and markets mix take the rate shock worse than WFC's lending mix. That is not what I underwrote, so if the September hike bid reverses I expect to give some of it back.

Short leg vs WFC, cut from 22.7 to 18.7 against a 19.0 long so the 0.77 and 0.76 betas still cancel to within 0.04% of NAV - the trim is beta-proportional so it does not convert a spread into a directional bank bet. Nothing is wrong with BAC and that has always been the point: EPS $4.33 up 27.7%, 2025 earnings $29.06bn up 14.6%, revenue $113.93bn trailing. I am short the price of an excellent franchise, not the franchise - at $62.32 and 14.4x, only 10.35% of headroom remains to a $68.77 target, and that headroom shrank again this week. New and specific to this leg: BAC announced a $250bn initiative to finance US data centres, energy, semiconductors and infrastructure, and agreed to buy 49.9% of Jio Credit for $1.9bn. Both are franchise-positive and both consume capital at a bank already trading two turns above the leg I am long. The risk I own is unchanged and real - an accelerating capital-markets cycle re-rates BAC past the sell side - which is exactly why this is beta-cancelled rather than an outright short, and why I have taken the whole pair down by a fifth after one good week rather than pressing it.

New pair, long leg vs V. This came off my original 150-name screen and I sized it at zero at entry because the spread was not stretched; it now is. MA/V sits at 1.560 against roughly 1.69 a year ago - Mastercard has trailed Visa by 8.3 points over twelve months, -2.5% against +5.8%. The reason was real and I underwrite it explicitly: MA's revenue growth decelerated to 15.8% then 14.1% across Q1-Q2 2026 while Visa's accelerated to 17.1% then 14.4%, inverting the growth premium. What makes this a trade rather than a value trap is that the market has now finished paying for that inversion. The traditional 3-5 turn Mastercard multiple premium is gone - 30.2x against 29.5x, or 32.74 against 32.49 on trailing - and at parity I am no longer paying anything for the faster compounder. MA still beat Q2 with $9.28bn revenue up 14% and adjusted EPS $5.04 up 21%, guided full-year net revenue to the high end of low double digits, and carries 12.46% upside to a $669.46 Strong Buy target against Visa's 9.83%. Bernstein, the most detailed work I found on the pair, prefers MA on 22.1% EPS momentum versus 10.2% and puts fair-value upside at +6.8% against -1.4%. Hedge quality is why this is the diversifier the book needed: betas 0.82 and 0.76, one of the highest daily-return correlations in the market, negligible two-year drift, both names at record highs so neither leg is a falling knife, and both report in late October within days of each other so the earnings event is close to common. Sized at 7% rather than large because the edge is genuine but modest - a 2.6-point target gap - and because Bernstein's own caveat is mine: if MA's deceleration continues, parity is the correct price and this spread simply sits.

New pair, short leg vs MA, sized 7.5 against 7.0 so the 0.76 and 0.82 betas cancel to within 0.04% of NAV - beta-matched, not dollar-matched. Visa is a superb business having a superb year and that is the whole reason it is the short: $381.60 against a $385.57 52-week high after closing at record levels on resilient consumer spending, 32.49x trailing, and only 9.83% left to a $418.92 target - the narrowest headroom of any leg in my book. Trailing revenue is $44.49bn up 14.4% and fiscal 2025 earnings $19.85bn, so I am shorting price and expectations, not execution. The asymmetry that made me pick the direction rather than coin-flip it is litigation: Visa absorbed $707m of interchange MDL provisions in Q1 FY26 and $899m in Q4 FY25 against Mastercard's $82m in Q2 2026, and the $200bn swipe-fee settlement got only preliminary approval on 09 June before the NRF, RILA and Walmart told the court they would rather go to trial. Structural interchange risk sits on both names in this duopoly, but it demonstrably lands harder on this one, and a trial outcome is the single event most likely to reopen the multiple gap in my favour. The risk I own is that Visa's growth acceleration persists and parity turns out to be the new equilibrium rather than an overshoot, which is why the whole pair is 14.5% of gross rather than a statement.

Long leg vs HD, held at 6.0. This was my worst pair of the week and I am neither adding nor cutting, which needs a reason on both counts. LOW fell 3.72% to $208.05 against HD's 1.61% and touched a six-week low; the mechanism was the rate shock, not company news - September hike odds jumped from 35% to 55% on Warsh, and LOW's DIY-discretionary mix carries housing-rate sensitivity that HD's Pro mix does not, so the common shock I expected to cancel instead moved the legs apart. Everything I underwrote got cheaper rather than weaker: LOW now trades at 17.59x with 22.26% upside to a $254.36 target against HD's 23.10x and 14.33%, a 7.9-point convergence gap versus 5.3 a week ago and a 5.5-turn multiple discount, and it sits $8.65 above its $199.40 52-week low. Sell-side framing hardened my way after both prints - Zacks #3 on LOW against #5 Strong Sell on HD, consensus growth ~9% against ~5% - and the board declared its $1.25 quarterly dividend on 08-28. A pure mean-reversion mandate would add into a spread this stretched with 0.88 daily-return correlation, betas 0.65 vs 0.68, 16 mean-crossings and -6% two-year drift. I do not add, because I halved this pair a week ago on a fundamental point that has not been retracted - LOW guided full-year sales and comps to the bottom end on persistent DIY softness while HD reaffirmed - and pressing into a stretch I myself argued was partly deserved would be doubling down against my own read. Holding is the honest middle between a widening spread and a fundamental I got wrong.

Short leg vs LOW, held at 5.7 against 6.0 so the 0.68 and 0.65 betas cancel to within 0.03% of NAV. I keep stating the evidence against this leg because it is still true: HD cleared the harder bar on 08-18 with $47.9bn of sales up 5.7%, comps +1.7% and adjusted EPS $4.92, and held full-year guidance through a housing slump with the CEO on medical leave. That is why the leg is half its original size rather than full. What keeps it on is price and the direction of the rate shock. At $330.19 HD is 23.10x with 14.33% upside to $377.50, five and a half turns richer than the leg I am long for four points less consensus growth, and it sits 23% below its $426.75 52-week high - this is not a stock the market is defending, it is one that has simply fallen less. If September brings the hike the futures now price at 55%, it hits housing turnover on both legs; the question my pair asks is whether five and a half turns of relative premium is the right compensation for HD's better Pro mix, and I think it is too much. No stop here, unchanged and deliberate: stopping out one side of a beta-matched pair leaves me naked long LOW into exactly the shock that triggered it, and with both companies a full quarter from their next print there is no dated event to stop against.

Long leg vs KLAC, held at 5.0 - nothing material changed. The ratio went 2.277 to 2.272 on the week, which after last week's 40% capture of the modelled convergence is exactly the pause a 34-day half-life implies; there is no new information to trade and churning a spread that is doing nothing just pays spread. TSM closed $417.52, down 2.29% on Friday's broad semis de-risking but only ~0.3% on the week, still at 28.44x - a large discount to the equipment names it supplies - with a $554.45 average target implying 32.8% upside and a Strong Buy consensus across 19 analysts, 2025 revenue up 31.6% and earnings up 46.6%, and the $100bn Arizona build extending the capacity story. The 15 mean-crossings and -12% two-year drift are unchanged, so last year's relative fall still reads as oscillation rather than decay. I keep this as the smallest pair in the book because it is the most violent, not because I doubt it.

Short leg vs TSM, held at 4.0 against a 5.0 long because KLAC's 2.70 beta still exceeds TSM's 2.15 - beta-matched, not dollar-matched. KLAC closed $183.77, essentially flat on the week after the prior week's 9.7% fall, so the spread neither extended nor retraced and there is nothing to act on. My position is unchanged and so is my discomfort with it: KLAC guided fiscal Q1 revenue and profit above consensus on AI infrastructure demand, so every dollar of the recent decline was multiple compression on improving fundamentals, and the cheap part of this short has already been paid. What holds the residual is that 50x trailing remains an extraordinary price for a cyclical whose 52-week range runs $83 to $307, and the target gap versus TSM has not closed to zero. This stays the smallest and most violent spread in the book on purpose - it is the leg most likely to be wrong fastest, which is why it is sized so being wrong costs the book almost nothing.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-29: Two things force my hand and they point the same way. First, my own audited rule: convergence gets taken rather than admired. WFC/BAC closed 35% of its target-gap in a single week, 8.1 points to 5.28 - that is the same trigger, at the same magnitude, that made me cut TSM/KLAC last week at 40% captured. If I book profit on a pair that works and hold full size on the one that works better, the rule is decoration. So WFC comes 23.0 to 19.0 and BAC 22.7 to 18.7, trimmed in beta-proportion so the cut does not quietly leave a directional bank bet. Second, concentration: WFC/BAC was 69% of gross, which meant I owned one spread wearing a diversified book's clothing. The trim plus a fourth pair takes it to 52% of gross and my largest single leg from 23% to 19%. I am not doing this to be smaller - gross rises 66.4% to 72.9% - I am doing it to be less singular. Where the money goes is long MA / short V, a pair from my original screen that I sized at zero because the spread was not stretched then and now is: MA has trailed V by 8.3 points over a year and the traditional 3-5 turn Mastercard multiple premium has gone to zero, while MA still compounds EPS at 22% against V's 10% and carries an order of magnitude less interchange-litigation provision. LOW/HD and TSM/KLAC hold. On LOW/HD specifically I am neither adding nor cutting, and I want the reason on the record: the spread widened against me on a rate shock, not on news, and everything I underwrote got cheaper - 7.9 points of target gap versus 5.3, a 5.5-turn discount, 9% versus 5% consensus growth. A mean-reversion mandate would normally add there. I do not, because I halved this pair a week ago on a fundamental point that has not been retracted - LOW guided to the bottom end while HD reaffirmed - and adding into a stretch I myself argued was fundamentally deserved would be doubling down against my own stated read. Holding is the honest position between those two facts. I carry no stops anywhere, unchanged and deliberate: a stop on one leg of a beta-matched pair does not reduce risk, it converts a spread into a naked directional position at the worst possible moment. Net SPY beta lands at about +0.06% of NAV rather than the mandate's +3.2%; with September hike odds at 55% I would rather run flatter than my brief than tilt long into it, and I state the deviation rather than bury it.
novelty: I manage only the Round-3 book this round, so the cross-round overlap rule does not bind me, but the new work is genuine: MA/V is a pair I screened at entry and deliberately sized at zero, brought on now for a specific reason - the Mastercard multiple premium has fully collapsed to Visa's while its EPS growth runs double Visa's - and it is the only leg in the book with no rate or housing sensitivity, which is precisely what a book carrying a bank pair and a home-improvement pair into a hawkish Fed needs.
research_notes:
Marks through 2026-08-28 close, all verified against stockanalysis.com/quote pages rather than memory.

WFC/BAC (my working pair): WFC $83.84 -> $86.69 (+3.40%), BAC ~$61.68 -> $62.32 (+1.04%). Relative +2.3% in my direction in one week. The measure I actually underwrote moved a lot: WFC's implied upside to a $100.24 target fell from 19.6% to 15.63% while BAC's to $68.77 fell from 11.5% to 10.35%, so the convergence gap closed from 8.1 points to 5.28 - roughly 35% of the gap captured in a week. WFC still 11% below its $97.76 52-week high at 12.6x on $6.88 EPS; BAC at 14.4x, $62.32 against a $65.23 52-week high. Neither reports until 13 Oct (confirmed), so nothing sits inside my horizon.

Macro, and it matters: Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole speech was the week's event. He said the better summer PCE/CPI prints "do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved"; futures moved September rate-HIKE odds from ~35% to ~55%, the 2-year to 4.35% and the 10-year to 4.72%. S&P 500 +0.5% on the week to 7,711.76, -0.25% Friday. This is a live regime item for two of my pairs and I treat it as such below rather than as noise.

LOW/HD (my losing pair): LOW $216.09 -> $208.05 (-3.72%), HD $335.61 -> $330.19 (-1.61%); ratio 0.6439 -> 0.6301, about 2.1% against me. LOW touched a six-week low. The mechanism is the rate shock, not a new fundamental: hike odds are directly hostile to housing turnover, and LOW's DIY-discretionary mix carries more of that than HD's Pro mix, so the common shock did not cancel cleanly. But the valuation evidence moved further my way, not against: LOW now 17.59x with 22.26% upside to $254.36, HD 23.10x with 14.33% upside to $377.50 - a 7.9-point gap versus 5.3 last week and a 5.5-turn discount. Sell-side framing has if anything hardened in my favour since the prints: Zacks #3 on LOW against #5 Strong Sell on HD, consensus earnings growth ~9% for LOW versus ~5% for HD. LOW declared its $1.25 quarterly dividend 08-28. Both are a full quarter from the next print.

TSM/KLAC: TSM $417.52 (-2.29% Friday, ~-0.34% on the week), KLAC $183.77 (~-0.12%). Ratio 2.277 -> 2.272 - flat. TSM 28.44x, Strong Buy, $554.45 target implying 32.8% upside; KLAC unchanged. The spread simply paused after last week's 40% capture.

New work - MA/V, which I screened at entry and never put on. MA $595.30, V $381.60, ratio 1.560. A year ago that ratio was ~1.69: MA has trailed V by 8.3 points over twelve months (-2.5% vs +5.8%). The reason is real and I want to be honest about it - MA's revenue growth decelerated to 15.8% then 14.1% in Q1-Q2 2026 while V's accelerated to 17.1% then 14.4%, so the growth premium that justified MA's multiple did invert. But the multiple has now fully repriced for it: 30.2x vs 29.5x, against a traditional 3-5 turn MA premium, and stockanalysis puts them at 32.74 vs 32.49. Meanwhile MA still beat Q2 with revenue $9.28bn +14% and adjusted EPS $5.04 +21%, guided FY net revenue to the high end of low-double-digit growth, and Bernstein has MA's EPS momentum at 22.1% versus V's 10.2% with fair-value upside +6.8% MA against -1.4% V. Target upside 12.46% MA vs 9.83% V. Litigation asymmetry favours the short leg too: V took $707m of interchange MDL provisions in Q1 FY26 and $899m in Q4 FY25 against MA's $82m in Q2 2026, and the $200bn swipe-fee settlement got only preliminary approval on 09 Jun before NRF, RILA and Walmart said they would rather go to trial. Hedge quality fits the mandate screen: betas 0.82 vs 0.76, both near 52-week highs so neither leg is a falling knife, and both report in late October within days of each other so the event is close to common. I checked XLU/D and the factor pair as alternatives and rejected both - shorting utilities into a hike scare would just stack the same rate bet I already carry through WFC/BAC.
